findings.summary: Run now lets cargo reach only the tree and the target directory, but the tree is `scratchpad/eddy-tree` inside the developer's checkout, so cargo cannot read the checkout's own `.cargo/config.toml` above the tree and exits on every Run.
findings.detail: Cargo looks for a `.cargo/config.toml` in every parent directory of where it runs. Landlock does not block `stat`, so cargo sees the repository root's `.cargo/config.toml` (a tracked file) as present. It then fails to read it with EACCES and stops with "could not load Cargo configuration ... Permission denied". With `.grant_write(self.root).grant_write(runner.target_dir)`, the guest's own directory (the developer's checkout) is no longer granted, so every `cargo build` or `cargo test` the reviewer or the reporter's repro check runs now fails before compiling anything. The same goes for `rust-analyzer scip` in `index`, which runs `cargo metadata` under `grant_write(root)` and `grant_write(dir)`. That is fatal through `succeed` when the baseline runs with symbols on. mise is protected by `MISE_CEILING_PATHS` in ENTER_TREE, but nothing stops cargo's walk up the parents. The new test only runs `sh` in `build/run-grants`, which has no `.cargo` above it, so it misses this. I could not build a reproduction: this review sandbox confines cargo the same way, so `cargo run --bin wado` itself failed with exactly that error (`failed to read configuration file /home/user/wado/.cargo/config.toml: Permission denied`). That shows how cargo behaves when an ancestor config cannot be read.
